summary: Read parent and child descriptions side by side

examined.reason: Implemented parent/child reading with equal panes and no empty detail placeholder. The active child remains the menu and agent selection; source and connection choices temporarily occupy the detail pane.

Implemented a shared valid-parent lookup with a reused menu identity index, paired rendering, and reading positions keyed by project/revision/description. Siblings preserve the visible parent position; depth and direct navigation use the actual parent.

Bound passage and contextual-link callbacks to the description owning them. Single links remain direct; choices remain beside their owning description, and cross-links construct the destination hierarchy.

Source from either visible description activates its owner and places it beside source. Closing restores that active description with its parent. Request cancellation prevents stale source responses from replacing a newer view; refresh checks that the source object is still current.

Implemented the proposed hierarchy pair, root/draft fallback, independent scrolling, source transitions, and singular active identity. Linked the parent resolver, shared pane renderer, and composition to the description; the desktop smoke checks the specified transitions.
The reader still connects broad explanations to detail and source; the root does not prescribe a single-description layout.
Stable identities, parent passage relationships, variable depth, and readable drafts already provide the data required to construct the pair.
Exact quote resolution applies independently to either visible description. Matching and repository boundaries need no change.

Updated style implementation for equal reading columns, independent overflow, single-pane states, and consistent metadata height. Existing inert text and Electron permission boundaries are unchanged; selectors now identify the current styles.
Updated the renderer selector after extracting shared description panes. Tests and Problems still show their existing content and source inspection behavior; the desktop smoke retains those checks.

Updated the implementation selector after moving description rendering into a shared pane function. Comparisons and selected passages are applied independently to each visible description; toggle behavior and text-comparison logic are unchanged.

results.method: npm run typecheck; npm run test:desktop; CLI validate; implementation and impact review
results.environment: Node v24.16.0; macOS arm64; real Electron desktop
results.evidence:
TypeScript typecheck passed. CLI validation reports no issues. The desktop smoke verifies actual parent/active panes, sibling/depth navigation, independent scroll positions and parent retention, source opening from active and parent descriptions, restoration on source close, cross-relationship navigation to the destination parent, root and broken-ancestry single-pane display, 300-leaf menus, history, inert content, individual test outcomes, syntax text preservation, and the restricted renderer API. The first development run checked a repaired fixture before its background reload completed; it failed with one sibling instead of two. The assertion now waits for the documented refresh to load the fixture. That failed output is retained in /private/tmp/stratic-pairs-smoke-first.txt. Reviewed source-request cancellation and identity-index reuse. Before/after snapshots match, and the impact frontier and uncovered renderer setup have explicit decisions. Backend unit tests were not rerun: project/review/Git logic is unchanged.
